topic: From Average Speed to Instantaneous Rate of Change: Understanding the Derivative

outline.topic: From Average Speed to Instantaneous Rate of Change: Understanding the Derivative

sections.title: The Problem of Average Speed
sections.content: Introduce the concept of average speed over an interval using the slope formula (rise/run). Visualize this on a position-time graph as a secant line connecting two points.
sections.example: A cheetah running: If it covers 100 meters in 5 seconds, its average speed is 20 m/s, but it didn't run at exactly that speed the whole time.

sections.title: The Shrinking Interval (The Intuitive Limit)
sections.content: Animate the second point on the graph moving closer to the first. Show the secant line morphing into a tangent line. Explain that as the time interval Δt approaches 0, the average speed becomes instantaneous speed.
sections.example: A GPS tracker on a race car: As you reduce the measurement interval from 1 second to 0.1s to 0.001s, the calculated speed converges to the speedometer reading at that exact moment.

sections.title: Defining the Derivative
sections.content: Formalize the concept using the limit notation: f'(x) = lim(h→0) [f(x+h) - f(x)] / h. Connect this algebra back to the visual 'slope of the tangent line' at a single point.
sections.example: Representing the curve as a path: The slope of the tangent line at any point on the curve represents the 'steepness' or rate of change of the function at that precise coordinate.

sections.title: Application: Prediction and Dynamics
sections.content: Summarize that the derivative tells us how a quantity changes at an exact instant. This is the foundation for predicting motion and optimization.
sections.example: A rocket launch: The derivative of its height function gives us the instantaneous velocity at any second, allowing engineers to know exactly when to trigger stage separation.

storyboard.title: The Problem of Average Speed
lecture_lines: Average speed is total distance over total time.
Visualize movement on a position-time graph.
A secant line connects two points on the graph.
animations: Display point A and point B on a curve in white (#FFFFFF).
Draw a secant line between points A and B in light blue (#00BFFF).
Show the formula for slope: m = Δy / Δx in yellow (#FFFF00).

storyboard.title: The Shrinking Interval (The Intuitive Limit)
lecture_lines: Move the second point closer to the first.
The secant line becomes a tangent line.
As the interval shrinks, we find instantaneous speed.
animations: Show point B approaching point A along the curve in green (#32CD32).
Animate the secant line flattening as the interval shrinks.
Emphasize the changing Δx as it nears zero in red (#FF4500).

storyboard.title: Defining the Derivative
lecture_lines: The derivative is a formal mathematical limit.
Slope of tangent equals the derivative at x.
It measures steepness at a single precise point.
animations: Display limit definition: lim (h→0) [f(x+h) - f(x)] / h in gold (#FFD700).
Flash the derivative notation f'(x) to label the limit.
Show the tangent line appearing at point A in white (#FFFFFF).

storyboard.title: Application: Prediction and Dynamics
lecture_lines: Derivatives show change at an exact instant.
They are essential for predicting dynamic motion.
Use them to optimize paths like rocket launches.
animations: Display a dynamic particle moving along the curve path.
Highlight the instantaneous velocity vector at specific points in cyan (#00FFFF).
Show the tangent slope predicting the next position in orange (#FFA500).
